svg.title: What the reflex compares when it asks whether a review already stands
svg.desc: Three lanes. At base the reflex compares the minted node ids, so a hand re-review of the same run and head is a different id, is not recognised, and a duplicate launches onto the identical review-store path. At the change it compares the pair (reviewed run, reviewed head): the same pair stands under any node id and the reflex dispatches nothing, while a run resumed to a new head is a different pair and gets exactly one review.
svg.text: A standing review is recognised by the run and head it read, not by the node id that read it
Measured 2026-09-26: a hand-dispatched re-review ran beside the reflex’s review of the same run, on the identical review-store paths.
at base: the key compared is the minted node id
both read the same pair: run r-...-source at head 3f2a91c4
the ids differ, so neither read recognises the other: the reflex launches a duplicate review of the very pair a review already stands for.
at the change: the key compared is the pair the review read
the pairs are equal whatever the node ids say
the reflex stands down: one review of this head, under either id.
and when the head moves: a review standing at the old head does not cover the new one
pairs differ, so exactly one review is dispatched at the new head.

Gate, 7 files, one invocation: 4 failed, 28 passed at base (2 added red, 2 pre-existing) → 2 failed, 30 passed at the change, zero added failures by id; the arm over the ids that pass at base exits 0.
Control: keying recognition on the node id again, the hand-dispatched case launches a duplicate review of the same pair and its assertion fails.
